v1_changes: ATH-11: core block FIRST by default in every session of every family (after the warm-up); about 2 core exercises (VOL-17); the user can move it after the plyos, after strength or to the end. Replaces the v0 'core primer only in athletic programs (tier 3b)' and 'core on optional days for hypertrophy' rules.

UNI-11 + ORD-06: pairing rule is slot-level and universal for any session that mixes lower and upper work - hip-dominant (posterior lower) goes with a push (anterior upper), knee-dominant goes with a pull - to avoid bleed-over. Applies to full body, bootcamps, athletic days, strength compressions and hybrid days.

ORD-06: BOOTCAMP 1 Tue/Fri ('Bilateral HD' -> 'Vertical Pull' -> 'Unilateral KD' -> 'Horizontal Push') was a mistake; corrected to hinge + horizontal push, single-leg squat + vertical pull. G2 grammar redefined.
UNI-11: the vertical vector is no longer 'free' - it follows the lower pattern it is paired with. G8 athletic themed days and HYBRID Saturday re-wired.

UNI-06: same-pattern days (squat + lunge) for physique / growth goals; cross-pattern days (squat + single-leg hinge) for bootcamp, fat loss, general fitness and athletes (default). Athletic default switched from the BYOP same-pattern grammar to cross-pattern; same-pattern kept as a variant for growth-focused athletes.
ORD-01: row before pulldown (horizontal before vertical) everywhere. The FAT BURN / 4 TRACKS / boxing pulldown-first order is not followed; open question 22 closed.
ORD-02: 'the work' (the day's main lift) comes first even when it is vertical (overhead-press weeks).
ORD-03: power before strength everywhere; the HYBRID 'strength before OLY' order is not followed; open question 18 closed.
ORD-04: calves first / side raises first only when that muscle is the client's priority; default position is the end of the session.

ORD-05: supersets are a fatigue and time tool with four use cases: short session, advanced athlete who needs more stimulus, off-season VO2max / mitochondrial work, beginner who does not fatigue. Default for an intermediate with enough time is straight sets.

ORD-07: 'the work' (main lift, 1 RIR) / 'the accessory' (supporting lift, 2 RIR) / 'the nuance' (weak point, unilateral or variation, MAX) / 'the survival' (isolation or joint health, done no matter what) confirmed as the strength backbone; strength cut order changed so the survival is never cut first.
ORD-08: a warm-up is always written (5 min any cardio + A March/Skip/Run or mobility); A-drills never count as volume.
ORD-09: fighters' cardio-first blocks are real aerobic blocks, not warm-ups.
ORD-10: optional days can be add-ons or separate days; separate is preferred.
ORD-11: Focus 1 and Focus 2 may hit the same muscle, 2-3 sets each, to bring a priority muscle up to its weekly target.

VOL-07: set-addition order (first exercise of the day first, then the next: 2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3); 3-4 exercises per muscle group per day; small muscles at the end get extra volume as a bonus exercise. Retires the v0 'at most 2 exercises per muscle per session'.

VOL-08 / VOL-16 / VOL-17 / UNI-09: exercise caps and session lengths by population (resistance-only 5-7, 45 min ~5, 60 min ~6-7, 75-90 min ~8-9; field athletes off-season up to 10-12 = 2 core + 2-4 plyo/ballistic + 2-3 Olympic/power + 3-4 resistance; athletes/bodybuilders/powerlifters ~90 min, max 2 h; general/weight loss 45-60 min). Replaces the v0 60-minute anchor for everyone.
VOL-17: calves 3 sets on every leg day; rear delts get their own sets (rear-delt station on pull days); about 2 core exercises.

PER-04: no axial (spinal) loading twice a week per pattern - one axial squat and one axial hinge a week; the second squat exposure is leg press / belt squat (EQ-11); the second hinge exposure is non-axial (pool PROPOSED).
PER-04: second weekly exposure of a slot uses a different exercise (confirmed), now constrained by the axial rule.
PRG-03: bootcamp = 4, 5 or 6 sessions a week, timed circuits of 5-7 stations x 3-5 rounds x 30-50 s, 35-45 min total. Bootcamp circuit day types added.
PRG-02: PPL weekdays are flexible (the athlete chooses).

PRG-05: level names L1 / L2 / L3; novice = newby (same thing) = under about 6-12 months of training; intermediate = consistent for over a year; more than 6-12 months off = body treated as L1 (skills return fast); ex-pros start L1 briefly.
PRG-06: one consistent algorithm for rep, set and volume progression across every level and model; templates carry no level-specific rep schemes.

PRG-07: notation '12/10/8 -20' = pyramid (12 mid weight, 10 heavier, 8 heaviest) then drop to a light 20-rep set (4 working sets); '10/10' = per side on unilateral work (1 set); '10/10' on a bilateral lift = two sets of 10.

FIX-03 / ATH-13: generic, understandable program and day names; 'JUSTICE LEAGUE' -> 'Athletic Performance - Non-Competitive' (weekend warriors, adults and youth). NO ACCESS meaning still pending (PRG-01 skipped).

ATH-07: aerobic sessions per week by population: 3 general / fat loss, 2 athletes in season, 4 aesthetics / bodybuilders + long walks after workouts (for the whole Muscle & Physique family; verification pass 2). Open question 8 closed except colour rules.

ATH-10 / ATH-09: every athletic session family carries Olympic work (L1: DB/KB snatch, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls / hang cleans; L2-L3: full lifts); youth may lift from the floor; older clients get few plyos unless they ask; no sex-based rules.

ATH-01 / ATH-02 / CAT-10: sport dial rebuilt on ground-contact time (long ground contact -> more ballistics, short -> more plyos); programs start more ballistic and become more plyometric; the plyo method progression (receive & pause -> receive then create -> repeated) is not a 'zone'.
ATH-04: boxers / strikers - pressing and arm volume is reduced (never cut to zero) when punching volume is high. v0 'H push and V pull removed' rule retired.
ATH-05 / EQ-06: no medball work for aesthetics / bodybuilders except as warm-up; medballs never over 20 lb.

ATH-06: COD stays for every athlete, tiered by turn angle; open question 12 closed. Generated athletic weeks carry COD from 60 min (hip days from 60, knee days from 75, 3-day S1 from 60 - verification pass 2).
ATH-12: contrast / French contrast for L2+ athletes off-season, about 78-85%, no rest inside the complex; open question 23 closed (keep the immediate format).
PER-05: deload = about half the sets, same exercises, lighter (or 3+ RIR), no buy-out or finisher; architecture kept. Open question 21 closed.

PER-01 / PER-02 / PER-03 / PER-07: plan shapes moved to 06 (4-6 week maintenance at ~50-70% volume, 8-week = 4 adapt + 4 drive, 12-week = 2-4 acclimate + 4-6 drive + hardest last weeks, week-by-week and yearly modes); A/B lead-lift weeks optional for variety seekers; tests by checkbox at block start or none.

UNI-02 / UNI-03 / UNI-10 / CAT-13: laterality dial added to lower (and upper) slots - bilateral:unilateral share from 90/10 to 10/90 by athlete, phase and pain; in season minimal bilateral; contralateral loading pulls into the hip (COD athletes), ipsilateral helps out of the hip (sprint acceleration).

VOL-09 / VOL-10 / UNI-01 / LIB-16: credit the exercise picked: helpers 0.25, dips 0.5 triceps / 0.5 chest, 10/10 unilateral = 1 set, athletic patterns (plyos, throws, Olympic lifts, sprints) never count toward muscle sets - so ballistic fills of the BASEBALL 'calfs' slot no longer count as calf sets.

EQ-01 / EQ-07 / EQ-08 / EQ-12 / LIB-09: no bands and no variable resistance in any pool (banded pulldowns, band assisted pull-ups, band chops removed); 'Camporini Deadlift' and 'strap rotating in/out' removed; 'Pull under' = lat pull-over.
VOL-10/VOL-11: 40-rep sets and AMRAPs only in CrossFit / hybrid styles.

All 30 generator split templates (2-6 days x 6 families) regenerated programmatically with these rules, plus variants (upper/lower, PPL x2, same-pattern athletic, BASEBALL Parts, in-season, bootcamp circuits). Each carries recomputed checks: weekly pattern frequency, slot-level pairing (UNI-11), axial budget (PER-04), core-first and H-before-V order, power before strength, exercise caps and a time estimate.

AP_PLYO.meaning: lower-body plyometric / jump (landing, box, hurdle, depth, repeat); upper plyo push-ups carry variant='upper'
AP_PLYO.v1_rule: plyo vs ballistic share by the sport's ground-contact time (ATH-01); programs start more ballistic then more plyometric; method progression receive & pause -> receive then create -> repeated receive/create (CAT-10, CAT-11 - not a zone); unilateral harder than bilateral; few plyos for older clients unless asked (ATH-09)

AP_JUMP_LIMITED_KNEE.meaning: ankle-stiffness / limited-knee hops, plate hops, jump rope
AP_JUMP_LIMITED_KNEE.library: F (copy) / G plate-hop block / C 'EASY' block

AP_SPRINT.meaning: sprint mechanics, accelerations, max velocity, A-drills
AP_SPRINT.v1_rule: speed sessions run squirrel jumps -> MACH drills / acceleration starts -> max velocity (LIB-21, RIGHT); sprints are the in-season stimulus for speed athletes (PER-08); never count toward muscle sets (VOL-10)

AP_THROW.meaning: medicine-ball throws (sagittal push/pull-down, rotational, step, half-kneeling into/out of hip)
AP_THROW.v1_rule: medball ballistic; none for aesthetics / bodybuilders except warm-up (ATH-05); never over 20 lb (EQ-06); no levels, just do them right (LIB-06); no medball -> plyo push-ups or no-ball slam, never band chops (EQ-07)

AP_COD.v1_rule: kept for every athlete, tiered by turn angle EASY -> MOD. -> HARD TURN (ATH-06); in the generated athletic weeks COD sits on hip (B) days from 60 min and knee (A) days from 75 min, and on the 3-day S1 from 60 min, so every athletic week from 60 min has COD (placement INFERRED, v1 verification pass 2)

AP_TRIPLE_EXT.meaning: triple extension / Olympic lifts and derivatives (pulls -> hang power -> full lifts)
AP_TRIPLE_EXT.v1_rule: everyone in athletic training gets Olympic work (ATH-10): L1 DB/KB snatch, hex-bar jumps, hang pulls / hang cleans; L2-L3 full lifts named 'Squat Snatch' / 'Squat Clean' / 'Squat Clean & Jerk' (LIB-07); youth may lift from the floor (ATH-09); older/injured never snatch (EQ-03); always before strength (ORD-03); never counts toward muscle sets (VOL-10)

ordering.science: SCIENCE: what is done first gets more reps and better quality (Simao et al. 2012) - supports power first, the work first and priority-muscle-first. INFERRED: a tiring core block could take quality away from the maximal jumps, sprints or Olympic lifts that follow; the coach places core first as a warm-up, so the generator keeps the first-position core block submaximal (PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL).

pairing.rule: In any session that mixes lower and upper work, a hip-dominant (posterior lower) pattern is paired with a push (anterior upper) and a knee-dominant pattern with a pull (posterior upper). The coach's reason: keep paired work as far apart as possible so fatigue does not bleed over, which lets the client do more total work across the week. Applies to full body, bootcamps, athletic days, strength compressions and hybrid days (ORD-06: 'That's the model that I'm using for full bodies and for boot camps').

supersets_and_complexes.generator_rule: Supersets are a fatigue and time tool (ORD-05). Use them when: (1) the session is short (30-45 min, or when added sets push a session past its length); (2) an advanced (L3) athlete or lifter needs more stimulus - the superset compresses the fatigue; (3) athletes in the off-season working on VO2max and mitochondrial capacity; (4) a beginner (L1) who is not getting fatigued by straight sets. An intermediate (L2) with enough time trains straight sets by default (INFERRED from the four cases). What to pair: the UNI-11 pairs (knee lift + pull, hip lift + push) and isolation pairs (e.g. biceps + rear delts, triceps + side delts, calves + delts). Never two lower compounds; never a heavy lift with a fatiguing lift for the same muscle, except contrast/French contrast for L2+ athletes off-season at about 78-85% with no rest inside the complex (ATH-12). Athletic families may use the BASEBALL grammar (Part C = bilateral lower + one upper compound, 'Superset - same reps'; Part D = unilateral + two isolations). Hybrid sessions do the paired accessory in the strength lift's rest period (OBSERVED HYBRID tri-sets).
supersets_and_complexes.time_overflow_rule: PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL: when week-by-week set additions (VOL-07) push a session past its length, first superset the lower/upper pairs (ORD-05 short-time case), then apply the cut order.

Where this differs from v1_rule (PER-05: about half the sets, same exercises, lighter or 3+ RIR, no buy-out or finisher), v1_rule governs; dropping the Olympic piece in a deload is OBSERVED, not a coach rule.
deload_test_architecture.v1_rule: Deload (PER-05): same exercises and architecture, about half the sets, lighter load or 3+ RIR, no buy-out or finisher. Tests (PER-07): chosen by checkbox at block start (strength, cardio, speed, or 'no need for testing'); when chosen, the final week holds a test day in place of one session. Plan shapes (PER-01, details in 06): 4-6 week maintenance/transition blocks at about 50-70% volume on the same templates; 8-week = 4 weeks adapting + 4 weeks driving hard, start hard; 12-week (preferred) = 2-4 weeks acclimation, 4-6 weeks hard, hardest last weeks; repeated 12-week cycles start one level higher; open week-by-week mode; yearly mode with quarter themes and holiday weeks in maintenance.
deload_test_architecture.retired_v0_rules: v0 '8 weeks = 7 building + week 8 test/deload', '12 weeks = 6 + deload + 5' and '6 weeks = 5 + deload/test' are retired by COACH-ANSWER PER-01 (NOT RIGHT). 4-6 week plans are maintenance / transition at about 50-70% volume; 8-week = 4 adapting + 4 driving hard; 12-week = 2-4 acclimation + 4-6 hard + hardest last weeks (details in 06).

laterality_dial.status: COACH-ANSWER UNI-02, UNI-03, UNI-10, UNI-08, CAT-13 (ranges and logic); default shares beyond his anchor points PROPOSED; the set math lives in 12_volume_algorithm_v1
laterality_dial.rule: Each lower (and upper) compound slot names a dominance; its laterality (bilateral or unilateral) is chosen so that the week's bilateral:unilateral share of sets matches the client's dial. Range 90/10 to 10/90. Unilateral work = health and rotational foundation; bilateral work = the driving force for size and strength.

anchors.bodybuilders / powerlifters: about 50/50 at the start of a program, moving to 80/20 - 90/10 bilateral; contralateral/ipsilateral unilateral work as health accessories mostly in the first 2-4 weeks, kept later only if something bothers them (UNI-02, CAT-13)
anchors.pain or injury: adjust accordingly; swapping a painful bilateral for a unilateral keeps the sets 'ideally' but is adjusted case by case (UNI-08, UNI-02)

laterality_dial.contra_ipsi: contralateral load pulls the athlete INTO the hip (COD athletes: football, soccer, basketball, tennis); ipsilateral helps OUT of the hip (sprint acceleration, e.g. ipsilateral step-ups) (CAT-13)
laterality_dial.slot_conversion: PROPOSED: convert bilateral stations to unilateral stations of the same dominance, starting with the second weekly exposure, until the share matches; keep at least one bilateral exposure a week off-season unless pain or in-season says otherwise.

axial_loading.status: COACH-ANSWER PER-04 (rule), EQ-11 (belt squat), EQ-03 (older/injured constrained machines); hinge pool and spacing PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL
axial_loading.rule: Load the spine once a week per pattern and load it correctly: one axial squat exposure and one axial hinge exposure a week. The second weekly squat exposure is a leg press or belt squat; deadlifts load the spine too, so the second hinge exposure is non-axial.
axial_loading.coach_words: 'I can do one day of squatting and the other day of leg pressing. I don't want to always load the lower back and the spine twice per week.' (PER-04)
axial_loading.axial_examples: barbell back / front / high-bar / low-bar / zercher / overhead / Smith squats; barbell or trap-bar deadlifts and RDLs; good mornings (INFERRED list)
axial_loading.non_axial_squat_pool: leg press, belt squat (COACH-ANSWER PER-04, EQ-11). Hack squat and pendulum are constrained machines the client may prefer (EQ-10, EQ-11 - machines are not ranked) but load the spine through shoulder pads, so they stay out of the pool until the coach says otherwise (INFERRED)
axial_loading.non_axial_hinge_pool: hip thrust (bar on the hips or machine), glute bridge, 45-degree back extension, reverse hyper, GHD hip extension, cable pull-through, KB swing as a ballistic hinge (PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL)
axial_loading.soreness_switch: if the athlete has already been loaded on the back that week, or is sore, switch to the belt squat (EQ-11)
axial_loading.spacing: PROPOSED: in 4-6 day A/B plans the axial squat sits on Monday (A1) and the axial hinge on Friday (B2), 4 days apart; Tuesday (B1) and Thursday (A2) are the non-axial exposures. Alternative: axial hinge on Tuesday.
axial_loading.check: every generated template counts axial exposures (checks.axial_exposures); all are <= 1 squat + 1 hinge
axial_loading.open: whether Olympic lifts, loaded jumps and light front-loaded bootcamp squats count toward the budget, and whether powerlifters are an exception (see open_questions)

set_addition.status: COACH-ANSWER VOL-07 (order), VOL-06 (rounding), VOL-04/VOL-05 (percent of weekly sets, chosen by the person's state - not by muscle size)
set_addition.exercises_per_muscle_per_day: about 3-4 exercises per muscle group per day (VOL-07); the v0 cap of 2 per muscle per session is retired
set_addition.order: when a muscle needs +1 set, add it to the FIRST exercise for that muscle in session order; the next added set goes to the second, then the third, then back to the first: 2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3 (equivalently: the exercise with the fewest sets, earliest first)
set_addition.why: 'I'm adding sets to the things that matter most... usually in the beginning... because I put all my energy into it' (VOL-07)
set_addition.small_muscle_bonus: a small muscle trained at the end of a long session (e.g. biceps after rows, pull-overs and pulldowns) gets its extra volume as a bonus exercise rather than more sets on a fatigued finisher (VOL-07); the generator uses the Focus slot (ORD-11) or the next session where that muscle is fresh (PROPOSED placement)
set_addition.weekly_rate: 3%, 5% or 7% of the muscle's weekly sets per week, picked by the person's state (fatigue, life, response) and adjustable by the coach; 10% a week is too much (VOL-05, UNI-05). Fractions are banked until they make a whole set (VOL-06). The percentage engine is in 12_volume_algorithm_v1.
set_addition.two_sessions_of_the_same_day_type: PROPOSED: when a day type appears twice a week (A1 Monday, A2 Thursday), added sets alternate between the two sessions so the weekly split stays even (open question)
set_addition.pseudo: def add_set(day, muscle): ex = [e for e in day.exercises if e.primary == muscle]; target = min(ex, key=lambda e: (e.sets, e.position)); target.sets += 1

roles_ORD07.the_work: the main lift, 1 RIR, first in the session (ORD-02)

Other families use role names work / paired_upper / secondary / iso that map onto it (PROPOSED mapping: work = the work; paired_upper and secondary = accessory; FOCUS and unilateral weak-point work = nuance; calves, rear delts and joint-health isolation = survival).
roles_ORD07.cut_order_consequence: because the survival is done no matter what, the strength cut order is now: cut the nuance first, then the accessory; keep the work and the survival

aesthetics.45: 5 exercises as 2 supersets + calves + rear delt on A days (~46 min); this is the 4-6-day A/B grammar - the 2-day days, 3-day Day C, upper/lower and PPL x2 days estimate ~50-60 min at 45 and go through the time-overflow rule (superset, then the cut order)
aesthetics.60: 7 stations / 8 exercises: 4 compounds straight, quad or ham isolation, [arm|delt] superset, calves (~63 min)
aesthetics.75: 8 stations straight (~64 min, leaves room for added sets)
aesthetics.90: 9 stations: 4 sets on compounds, Focus (lead or priority muscle), longer rests (~90 min)

athletic.45: core, plyo, throw, Olympic, [work|pull] and [unilateral|press] supersets, calves (~48 min)
athletic.60: core 2 + plyo + throw + COD on hip (B) days + Olympic + 4 compounds + <calves 3 + rear delt> on knee days at 2 sets (~58-64 min)
athletic.75: + COD on knee (A) days, hamstring curl, buy-out
athletic.90: + 2nd plyo or sprint, 3 sets per slot: 11 exercises / 10 stations (~97 min)

strength.60: the work + the nuance + the survival (+ accessory if time)
strength.90: all four roles + calves / rear delts (~56-65 min for the 4-day days; leaves rest time for heavy work)

fat_loss_bootcamp.45: gym: 5 exercises as 2 supersets + calves (+ rear delt on A days) (~42-46 min); circuit: 5-7 stations, 35-45 min

hybrid_crossfit.60: warm-up, core, skill, Olympic, [strength|pull or push] with calves in the strength lift's rest on leg days, [unilateral|upper], rear delt once a week, WOD 12 min (~56-64 min)
hybrid_crossfit.90: + calves as their own station, longer skill and WOD (~75-86 min); aerobic add-ons only on 2-hour days

no_equipment.45: as fat loss gym or circuit, bodyweight pools
no_equipment.60: as fat loss gym, bodyweight pools

science_notes: SCIENCE: per-set durations assume 30-60 s of work and the coach's own rests (1-2 min hypertrophy, 3-6 min strength); agonist-antagonist / non-competing pairing roughly halves rest overhead without hurting volume load (Robbins et al. 2010, JSCR; Weakley et al. 2017, EJAP; Iversen et al. 2021, Sports Med)

SCIENCE (weak): a per-session ceiling of roughly 6-10 hard sets per muscle is an RP practitioner heuristic with limited direct trial evidence; Schoenfeld et al. 2017 is a WEEKLY dose-response meta-analysis and does not support a per-session cap. The coach's habit of adding other qualities to long sessions is OBSERVED behaviour, not derived from this.

SCIENCE: exercise order effects - movements done first get more reps and quality (Simao et al. 2012, Sports Med), supporting 'priority first' (athletic first; calves/delts first when they are the priority)

SCIENCE: per-session sets per muscle - the dose-response for hypertrophy flattens within a session at around 6-11 hard sets per muscle (practitioner landmarks; weak direct trial evidence). Same-pattern days (squat + lunge + leg extension) put 8-11 quad sets in one session at 90 min, which sits inside that range; the volume engine (12) owns the weekly numbers.
session_length_model.headroom_note: Starting sessions sit at or slightly above their length at week 1; set additions (VOL-07) later push them over, which triggers the time-overflow rule (supersets first, then the cut order) - PROPOSED.

aesthetics.family_notes: Muscle & physique. SAME-pattern days (squat + lunge; hinge + single-leg hinge) to drive the muscle harder (COACH-ANSWER UNI-06). Knee days carry the pulls, hip days the pushes (UNI-11). Core first (ATH-11). Calves 3 sets every leg day, rear delts their own sets (VOL-17). Axial squat once and axial hinge once a week (PER-04). Session length 45-60 min for general clients, about 90 min for bodybuilders (UNI-09); 5-7 exercises (VOL-16), 8-9 at 75-90 min (VOL-08). No medball work except as warm-up (ATH-05). Aerobic: 4 sessions a week + long walks after workouts for aesthetics / bodybuilding clients (ATH-07: '4 for aesthetics bodybuilders'; the v1 split that gave general physique clients 3 was withdrawn in verification pass 2).

sport_dial.ground_contact_model: The longer a sport keeps the athlete on the ground, the more ballistics and the fewer plyos; the shorter, the more plyos (ATH-01). Both ends are always present. Programs start more ballistic and become more plyometric over the block (CAT-10).
sport_dial.plyo_ranking_ATH02: basketball ~ volleyball > sprinters > football skill positions > soccer > MMA > tennis > baseball > hockey > wrestling/BJJ > boxing ~ karate > golf (COACH-ANSWER ATH-02, RIGHT)

basketball / volleyball.frontal_transverse: more lateral lunges / cossacks / rotational lunges (UNI-12)

MMA / fighters / karate / boxing.plyo_vs_ballistic: more ballistics, fewer plyos (long ground contact) - some plyos always for tissue strength
MMA / fighters / karate / boxing.pressing: reduce pressing and arm volume when punching volume is high - never cut it all the way (ATH-04)
MMA / fighters / karate / boxing.aerobic: cardio-first blocks are real aerobic work (ORD-09)
MMA / fighters / karate / boxing.frontal_transverse: more lateral / rotational unilateral work (UNI-12: more for basketball, tennis, soccer and MMA)

generator_algorithm: 1 INPUTS: goal family, days per week (2-6), session minutes (30/45/60/75/90; PROPOSED 105/120 for competitive athletes, UNI-09), experience level L1/L2/L3 (PRG-05), equipment, sport + position + season if competitive (GEN-02), body weight, plan type (4-6 maintenance / 8 / 12 / week-by-week / yearly - PER-01), priority muscles, pain areas, rep-style preference, laterality dial overrides, coach-added rules (GEN-08).

2 WEEK: take generator_split_templates[family][days].week_layout (or the variant the sport / phase / preference selects: same-pattern athletic, BASEBALL Parts, in-season, upper/lower, PPL x2 with flexible weekdays, bootcamp circuit). Optional days separate by default, add-on if the client prefers (ORD-10). Place the aerobic sessions per ATH-07.
3 SESSIONS: for each day type keep stations with include_from_minutes <= minutes; resolve sets ranges; warm-up always (ORD-08); core block first unless the user moved it (ATH-11).

4 PAIRING + SUPERSETS: keep the UNI-11 pairs (hip + push, knee + pull); superset them when the session is short, the athlete is L3 wanting more stimulus, the athlete is off-season doing VO2max/mitochondrial work, or the client is an L1 who does not fatigue (ORD-05); otherwise straight sets.

5 ORDER: warm-up -> core block -> plyo/ballistic -> throws -> COD -> Olympic/power (ORD-03) -> the work (ORD-02) + paired upper -> secondary pairs (H before V, ORD-01) -> isolation (small muscle first only if priority, ORD-04) -> conditioning (fighter aerobic blocks may open the day, ORD-09).

6 VALIDATE THE WEEK: pattern frequency invariant; slot-level pairing; axial budget <= 1 squat + 1 hinge (PER-04); each upper vector >= 1x; calves 3 sets each leg day and at least one rear-delt station a week at the chosen length (VOL-17); aerobic sessions per ATH-07 (aerobic_ATH07); exercise cap and time estimate per population (VOL-08, UNI-09, PRG-03); >= 1 OFF day; coach-added rules (GEN-08).

7 FILL: default exercise per slot + dropdown of swaps in the same category (GEN-04); filter by level (levels add options, CAT-05), equipment (no bands / no variable resistance, EQ-01, EQ-12), pain (machines / split grips / drop, VOL-03) and client preference (EQ-10); older/injured/high-volume -> constrained machines, never overhead squat / snatch / low-bar / depth jumps (EQ-03); second weekly exposure = different exercise, non-axial for squats and hinges (PER-04); laterality dial sets bilateral vs unilateral (UNI-02).

8 DOSE: starting weekly sets per muscle by level and goal from the volume engine (03 / 12); credit the exercise picked: primary 1.0, helpers 0.25 (VOL-09), dips 0.5/0.5 (LIB-16), 10/10 = 1 set (UNI-01), athletic patterns 0 (VOL-10); RIR as the effort language (VOL-13); rests 1-2 (up to 3) min hypertrophy, 3-6 min strength (VOL-14).

9 PROGRESS: weekly +3/5/7% of the muscle's sets chosen by the person's state (VOL-05), banked to whole sets (VOL-06), added in session order 2/2/2 -> 3/2/2 -> 3/3/2 -> 3/3/3 -> 4/3/3 (VOL-07), small-muscle bonus exercise (VOL-07); adjust from logged effort / how it felt (GEN-05) only when the user chooses to log - the coach is unsure whether tracking belongs in the tool (GEN-03), so without logs the plan follows its preset progression (PROPOSED - PENDING COACH APPROVAL); if a session overflows its length, superset first, then cut (PROPOSED).

10 PERIODISE: block 4-6 weeks with small variable changes between blocks (PER-02); 8-week = 4 adapt + 4 drive; 12-week = 2-4 acclimate + 4-6 hard + hardest last weeks; repeated cycles start one level higher; 4-6 week maintenance at ~50-70% volume; deload = ~half the sets, same architecture, no finisher (PER-05); tests by checkbox or none (PER-07); A/B lead-lift weeks optional (PER-03). Details in 06.
